# M1c legacy wire golden

`m1c-legacy-wire-golden.json` freezes the raw UTF-8 request-body SHA-256 and byte length for two existing compatibility tests. It replaces a dependency on an untracked, full M1c plugin bundle; it is not a new production protocol.

## Provenance

- Original plugin build: `5efe9302a36e3d90`.
- Original plugin SHA-256: `f1d3eba681c389ccffb83fe51a6f30b4d321bc86799f553014a32e83381c2117`, checked before capture.
- Capture used the original test helpers at commit `b330b89c46819813945b4ce3a021466b66e0895e`, Node 24.16.0 and synthetic transport callbacks; no provider requests.
- The fixture records the capture test and mixed-language input fixture hashes. Existing input literals, including historical encoding artifacts, are intentionally unchanged.
- `serializerBudgetFallback`: the existing `captureBudgetFallback` input (header plus 4,000 repeats); the full request body is 57,652 UTF-8 bytes.
- `manualCompatibilityFallback`: the existing `original14Markdown` manual input. The original M1c call succeeded with exactly one request, whose full body is 4,619 UTF-8 bytes. The current malformed-response scenario must use exactly two requests and its second body must match this oracle.

The tests continue to execute the current plugin and retain display, cache-write and ledger assertions. Hash the exact captured body string: do not parse, normalize line endings, reorder JSON, remove fields or re-serialize it before comparison.

## Update policy

This is an independent regression oracle, not a snapshot generated by the current implementation. Normal test runs must not rewrite it. If the compatibility contract is deliberately changed, review that change and replace the oracle from an independently pinned reference with fresh provenance. Do not silence a mismatch by copying the current request digest into this file.

Raw capture material and the old plugin belong outside Git. Running these tests needs neither that plugin nor a local artifacts directory. A checksum mismatch is a wire-contract change; use the assertion name to distinguish byte-length drift from same-length content drift.

## Re-freeze 2026-09-13

- `protectAutoTechnicalTerms` no longer guesses all-caps tokens as acronyms (user decision: acronyms are pinned with protected terms instead). In the `original14Markdown` manual-compatibility body the token `GED` now travels as text instead of a placeholder, so the frozen legacy body shrank from 4,619 to 4,615 UTF-8 bytes and its SHA-256 changed.
- Re-captured with the same test helper (`captureManualCompatibility`) on the current bundle; build id, bundle SHA-256 and Node version are recorded under `provenance.refreeze`.
- `serializerBudgetFallback` is untouched: its input has no all-caps token, and the test still passes against the original M1c bytes.

## Re-freeze 2026-09-14

- The user translation preferences (settings, "AI translation preferences") now travel with every AI request, including the legacy whole-message wire. Both frozen legacy bodies gained the fixed preference block that carries the default preferences of the test interface language (English): `serializerBudgetFallback` 57,652 -> 58,316 bytes, `manualCompatibilityFallback` 4,615 -> 5,279 bytes.
- The decision rules for AI decision mode moved from the editable template into fixed code (`LEGACY_DECISION_RULES`); neither frozen body runs in AI decision mode, so the block is the only change. Re-captured with the same test helpers on the current bundle; build id, bundle SHA-256 and Node version are recorded under `provenance.refreezes[1]`.
